sn22.1:5.5: ‘Sir, I’m an old man, elderly and senior. I’m advanced in years and have reached the final stage of life. My body is ailing and I’m constantly unwell.
sn22.1:5.6: I hardly ever get to see the esteemed mendicants.
sn22.1:5.7: May the Buddha please advise me
sn22.1:5.9: It will be for my lasting welfare and happiness.’
sn22.1:6.1: When I said this, sir, the Buddha said to me:
sn22.1:6.2: ‘That’s so true, householder! That’s so true, householder!
sn22.1:6.3: For this body is ailing, swaddled in its shell.
sn22.1:6.4: If anyone dragging around this body claimed to be healthy even for an hour, what is that but foolishness?
sn22.1:6.5: So you should train like this:
sn22.1:6.6: Though my body is ailing, my mind will be healthy.
